title: DBKL told to brief PM on flood mitigation measures in capital — FT minister - The Edge Malaysia
text:
DBKL told to brief PM on flood mitigation measures in capital — FT minister Monday 16 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 16): Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has reduced the number of flash flood hotspots in the capital from 31 in 2022 to 14 this year, and aims to cut the figure further to 10 by year-end through ongoing mitigation measures.
 Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the initiative was among the measures introduced by DBKL following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's directive to prioritise solutions to flash flooding through cooperation with the Department of Irrigation and Drainage and a review of best practices in flood management by the city authority.
 She said all DBKL branch offices in Kuala Lumpur's parliamentary constituencies must provide real-time reports to the mayor whenever it rains, enabling immediate coordinated action.
 She said two task forces were also focusing on enhancing flood mitigation efforts and turning open spaces into water-absorbing areas in line with the sponge city concept.
 “In cities, floods can result in extensive damage to property and put lives at risk. Therefore, our efforts are coordinated and carried out regularly, not just when the northeast monsoon is imminent,” she said at a press conference following the Federal Territories state disaster management committee meeting here on Monday.
 She said 4,162 personnel from various Federal Territories agencies were ready to respond to any eventuality, with 139 lorries, 60 boats and 144 four-wheel-drive vehicles at their disposal.
 Hannah also said 120 temporary relief centres have been prepared, with capacity to accommodate up to 31,000 flood victims at once.
 Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Fadlun Mak Ujud said DBKL had allocated RM27 million for next year to continue efforts to reduce the number of flash flood hotspots to 10 or fewer.
 He said DBKL now carries out maintenance on drainage systems, rivers and retention ponds quarterly, up from twice a year.
 During the monsoon season, maintenance would be stepped up to every two months to clear sediment and maximise water flow, with seven contractors handling drainage systems and 12 maintaining retention ponds, he said.
 Fadlun said roadside drainage inlets would also be modified to improve rainwater flow into the drainage network.
 He said DBKL has also deployed 180-horsepower pumps at 10 low-lying areas to pump excess water into rivers.
 According to him, DBKL has completed nine on-site detention (OSD) ponds, is building six more and plans another six in 2027, is monitoring more than 65 privately developed ponds, and has completed a 1.3km flood barrier.
 Fadlun said DBKL had also activated an operations room to monitor weather conditions, obtain forecasts one to two hours in advance, coordinate response efforts and issue early warnings to residents in flood-prone areas.
